record.context_brief: Almost-greedy versus semi-greedy in quasi-Banach spaces
record.original_question: In a quasi-Banach space, does the equivalence between almost-greedy bases and semi-greedy bases remain true for general Markushevich bases, without assuming that the basis is Schauder? Here, almost-greedy means that greedy projections approximate as well as the best coordinate projections up to a uniform constant, while semi-greedy means that for each greedy set A, the best approximation inside span{x_n : n in A} is bounded by a constant times the best |A|-term approximation error.

evidence.quote: Definition 4.8 We say that a Markushevich basis B in a quasi-Banach space X is almost-greedy if there is a positive constant C such that for every x in X, ||x - P_A(x)|| <= C inf_{|B|<=|A|} ||x - P_B(x)||, whenever A is a finite greedy set of x.

Definition 4.14 Let B be a Markushevich basis in a quasi-Banach space X. We say that the basis is semi-greedy if for every x in X, there exists a constant C such that min (||x - sum_{n in A} a_n x_n|| : a_n in F, forall n in A) <= C sigma_{|A|}(x), whenever A is any finite greedy set of x.
Theorem 4.17 Let B be a Schauder basis in a quasi-Banach space. The basis is semi-greedy if and only if the basis is almost-greedy.
Question 3. Is it possible to remove the condition of Schauder in the characterization of semi-greediness in quasi-Banach spaces?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a quasi-Banach space over the scalar field $\mathbb{F}\in\{\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C}\}$, and let $\mathcal{B}=(x_n)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ be a Markushevich basis of $X$ (that is, $(x_n)$ is a complete and minimal sequence with biorthogonal functionals $(x_n^*)$ that separate the points of $X$). For each $x\in X$ and each finite set $A\subset\mathbb{N}$, define the coordinate projection $P_A(x)=\sum_{n\in A}x_n^*(x)\,x_n$. A finite set $A$ is called a greedy set of $x$ (of cardinality $|A|$) if $\min_{n\in A}|x_n^*(x)|\ge\max_{n\notin A}|x_n^*(x)|$. Define the best $m$-term approximation error
$$\sigma_m(x)=\inf\Bigl\{\Bigl\|x-\sum_{n\in B}a_n x_n\Bigr\|:\ B\subset\mathbb{N},\ |B|\le m,\ a_n\in\mathbb{F}\Bigr\}.$$
The basis $\mathcal{B}$ is called almost-greedy if there is a constant $C>0$ such that $\|x-P_A(x)\|\le C\,\sigma_{|A|}(x)$ for every $x\in X$ and every finite greedy set $A$ of $x$. The basis $\mathcal{B}$ is called semi-greedy if there is a constant $C>0$ such that for every $x\in X$ and every finite greedy set $A$ of $x$,
$$\min\Bigl\{\Bigl\|x-\sum_{n\in A}a_n x_n\Bigr\|:\ a_n\in\mathbb{F}\Bigr\}\le C\,\sigma_{|A|}(x).$$
It is known that when $\mathcal{B}$ is additionally a Schauder basis of $X$, $\mathcal{B}$ is almost-greedy if and only if it is semi-greedy. 

Question: Does this equivalence persist for general Markushevich bases in quasi-Banach spaces without assuming the Schauder property? In other words, is every semi-greedy Markushevich basis in a quasi-Banach space necessarily almost-greedy (and vice versa)?
artifact.status_search_result: The equivalence is established for Schauder bases in quasi-Banach spaces and for Markushevich bases in Banach spaces (Berasategui–Berná–Lassalle, J. Fourier Anal. Appl. 2023). However, no published result removes the Schauder assumption in the quasi-Banach setting. Recent works on greedy approximation in quasi-Banach spaces (2025) continue to list this characterization only under Schauder hypotheses, indicating the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Weak Greedy Algorithms and the Equivalence Between Semi-greedy and Almost Greedy Markushevich Bases
status_evidence.snippet: In infinite dimensional Banach spaces, the notions of semi-greedy, branch semi-greedy, weak semi-greedy, and almost greedy Markushevich bases are equivalent.
status_evidence.claim: Equivalence proved for Markushevich bases in Banach spaces, not the quasi-Banach setting.

status_evidence.title: Lebesgue-type estimates for greedy algorithms in quasi-Banach spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Recent investigations into greedy approximation properties in quasi-Banach spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent quasi-Banach work does not establish the equivalence beyond Schauder bases.

status_evidence.title: When Greedy Approximation Breaks: Counterexamples in Quasi-Banach Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Counterexamples illustrating the subtleties of greedy-type bases in quasi-Banach spaces.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the open question in the quasi-Banach Markushevich case is reported.
